item.title: Undertone 1.18.19
item.description:
• Buy credits. Out of free credits? Buy a credit pack from the credits sheet: 500, 1,300 or 2,800 credits. They never expire.
  • The beta ends on Friday, November 6. Until then everything in Pro stays free.

Undertone 1.18.18

  • Free credits now last about a week. New accounts start with 1,000 credits instead of 100.
  • Meeting prep, people look-ups and calendar checks use the faster model on free credits, so background work no longer eats the credits meant for your calls and Ask.

Undertone 1.18.17

Undertone learns from each day

  • Every evening (or the next time you open it), Undertone looks back over the day's work meetings, Ask chats and ratings.
  • It remembers new facts (who owns what, decisions, deadlines) and drops ones that are now out of date.
  • It corrects term meanings it got wrong or too generic, and looks up terms that are still unclear in your sources.
  • It stops hinting terms you clearly know, and keeps a few lessons that shape tomorrow's hints, answer cards and Ask answers.
  • See what it learned on Home under "What Undertone learned", or press "Review now". Turn it off in Settings › "Learn from each day".

Undertone 1.18.16

A tidier setup. The "Pick your sources" step now uses the same tabs as Settings: Connected, Claude connectors and Add a source, instead of one long list.

Undertone 1.18.15

Task chats learn from you. When you're working on a task in Ask and tell it something new, like "this is a DM to Mike", Undertone saves that to memory and rewords the task to match. A small "Task updated" note shows what changed.

Drafts look right. Copy-ready messages now show bold, italics, code and links instead of raw * and <url|title> markup. Copy keeps that formatting when you paste into Slack, Mail or Docs.

"Say more" is now "Elaborate".

Undertone 1.18.8

Terms ready when you open them. During a call, each new term is looked up in your sources in the background, one at a time, so clicking it shows the people, links and context right away. Looking one up by hand is faster too. Turn it off in Settings › Hints if you like.

One recap per meeting. When Undertone updates or quits mid-call, the meeting carries on and gets a single recap at the end, instead of one at every restart.

Fewer answer cards in presentations. No cards for a presenter's own questions, or for "what is X?" when X is already explained.

A minimized panel that's yours. Drag it anywhere on screen. It's now Tide, a small disc whose water rises while people talk and whose rim turns blue when a question is for you. Five more styles are in Settings › Minimized panel: Waterline, Edge tab, Ticker, Halo and Surface.
